[164](https://docs.rs#164)//! # Implementation
[165](https://docs.rs#165)//!
[166](https://docs.rs#166)//! Files are read using [`include_bytes!`]. This normally places data in
[167](https://docs.rs#167)//! `__TEXT,__const`, where immutable data is kept. However, property list data
[168](https://docs.rs#168)//! is expected to be in `__TEXT,__info_plist` or `__TEXT,__launchd_plist`. This
[169](https://docs.rs#169)//! section will explain how I accomplish that.
[170](https://docs.rs#170)//!
[171](https://docs.rs#171)//! We begin by reading the file from disk:
[172](https://docs.rs#172)//!
[173](https://docs.rs#173)//! ```rust
[174](https://docs.rs#174)//! const BYTES: &[u8] = include_bytes!("Info.plist");
[175](https://docs.rs#175)//! ```
[176](https://docs.rs#176)//!
[177](https://docs.rs#177)//! A naïve approach is to do the following:
[178](https://docs.rs#178)//!
[179](https://docs.rs#179)//! ```rust
[180](https://docs.rs#180)//! # const BYTES: &[u8] = &[];
[181](https://docs.rs#181)//! #[used] // Prevent optimizing out
[182](https://docs.rs#182)//! #[link_section = "__TEXT,__info_plist"]
[183](https://docs.rs#183)//! static PLIST: &[u8] = BYTES;
[184](https://docs.rs#184)//! ```
[185](https://docs.rs#185)//!
[186](https://docs.rs#186)//! This doesn't work because only the slice's pointer and length that are
[187](https://docs.rs#187)//! placed in `__TEXT,__info_plist`. The referenced bytes are still placed in
[188](https://docs.rs#188)//! `__TEXT,__const`.
[189](https://docs.rs#189)//!
[190](https://docs.rs#190)//! Instead, we need to arrive at the following:
[191](https://docs.rs#191)//!
[192](https://docs.rs#192)//! ```rust
[193](https://docs.rs#193)//! # const N: usize = 0;
[194](https://docs.rs#194)//! # const BYTES: &[u8; N] = &[];
[195](https://docs.rs#195)//! #[used]
[196](https://docs.rs#196)//! #[link_section = "__TEXT,__info_plist"]
[197](https://docs.rs#197)//! static PLIST: [u8; N] = *BYTES;
[198](https://docs.rs#198)//! ```
[199](https://docs.rs#199)//!
[200](https://docs.rs#200)//! We can get `N` by using [`len`]. As of Rust 1.39, it is possible to get the
[201](https://docs.rs#201)//! length of a slice within a `const`.
[202](https://docs.rs#202)//!
[203](https://docs.rs#203)//! ```rust
[204](https://docs.rs#204)//! # const BYTES: &[u8] = &[];
[205](https://docs.rs#205)//! const N: usize = BYTES.len();
[206](https://docs.rs#206)//! ```
[207](https://docs.rs#207)//!
[208](https://docs.rs#208)//! The next step is to dereference the bytes into a `[u8; N]`.
[209](https://docs.rs#209)//!
[210](https://docs.rs#210)//! There are two approaches:
[211](https://docs.rs#211)//!
[212](https://docs.rs#212)//! 1. <span id="approach-1"></span>Call [`include_bytes!`] again.
[213](https://docs.rs#213)//!
[214](https://docs.rs#214)//!    This is not the approach used by this library because of concerns about
[215](https://docs.rs#215)//!    compile performance. See the [second approach](#approach-2) for what this
[216](https://docs.rs#216)//!    library does.
[217](https://docs.rs#217)//!
[218](https://docs.rs#218)//!    The following is all we need:
[219](https://docs.rs#219)//!
[220](https://docs.rs#220)//!    ```rust
[221](https://docs.rs#221)//!    # const BYTES: &[u8] = include_bytes!("Info.plist");
[222](https://docs.rs#222)//!    # const N: usize = BYTES.len();
[223](https://docs.rs#223)//!    #[used]
[224](https://docs.rs#224)//!    #[link_section = "__TEXT,__info_plist"]
[225](https://docs.rs#225)//!    static PLIST: [u8; N] = *include_bytes!("Info.plist");
[226](https://docs.rs#226)//!    ```
[227](https://docs.rs#227)//!
[228](https://docs.rs#228)//!    This works because `include_bytes!` actually returns a `&[u8; N]`. It's
[229](https://docs.rs#229)//!    often used as a `&[u8]` because we don't know the size when calling it.
[230](https://docs.rs#230)//!
[231](https://docs.rs#231)//! 2. <span id="approach-2"></span>Dereference our current bytes through
[232](https://docs.rs#232)//!    pointer casting.
[233](https://docs.rs#233)//!
[234](https://docs.rs#234)//!    This is tricker than the [first approach](#approach-1) (and somewhat
[235](https://docs.rs#235)//!    cursed). If you know me, then it's predictable I'd go this route.
[236](https://docs.rs#236)//!
[237](https://docs.rs#237)//!    We can get a pointer to the bytes via [`as_ptr`], which is usable in
[238](https://docs.rs#238)//!    `const`:
[239](https://docs.rs#239)//!
[240](https://docs.rs#240)//!    ```rust
[241](https://docs.rs#241)//!    # const BYTES: &[u8] = &[];
[242](https://docs.rs#242)//!    # const N: usize = 0;
[243](https://docs.rs#243)//!    const PTR: *const [u8; N] = BYTES.as_ptr() as *const [u8; N];
[244](https://docs.rs#244)//!    ```
[245](https://docs.rs#245)//!
[246](https://docs.rs#246)//!    Unfortunately, this pointer can't be directly dereferenced in Rust 1.39
[247](https://docs.rs#247)//!    (minimum supported version).
[248](https://docs.rs#248)//!
[249](https://docs.rs#249)//!    ```compile_fail
[250](https://docs.rs#250)//!    # // This may work in future versions, so we intentionally make this
[251](https://docs.rs#251)//!    # // always fail to compile so long as our MSRV is 1.39.
[252](https://docs.rs#252)//!    #[used]
[253](https://docs.rs#253)//!    #[link_section = "__TEXT,__info_plist"]
[254](https://docs.rs#254)//!    static PLIST: [u8; N] = unsafe { *PTR };
[255](https://docs.rs#255)//!    ```
[256](https://docs.rs#256)//!
[257](https://docs.rs#257)//!    Instead, we must cast the pointer to a reference.
[258](https://docs.rs#258)//!
[259](https://docs.rs#259)//!    You may want to reach for [`transmute`], which was stabilized for use in
[260](https://docs.rs#260)//!    `const` in Rust 1.46. However, earlier versions need to be supported, so
[261](https://docs.rs#261)//!    that is not an option for this library.
[262](https://docs.rs#262)//!
[263](https://docs.rs#263)//!    This bitwise cast can be accomplished with a `union`:
[264](https://docs.rs#264)//!
[265](https://docs.rs#265)//!    ```rust
[266](https://docs.rs#266)//!    # const BYTES: &[u8] = &[];
[267](https://docs.rs#267)//!    # const N: usize = 0;
[268](https://docs.rs#268)//!    # const PTR: *const [u8; N] = BYTES.as_ptr() as *const [u8; N];
[269](https://docs.rs#269)//!    union Transmute {
[270](https://docs.rs#270)//!        from: *const [u8; N],
[271](https://docs.rs#271)//!        into: &'static [u8; N],
[272](https://docs.rs#272)//!    }
[273](https://docs.rs#273)//!
[274](https://docs.rs#274)//!    const REF: &[u8; N] = unsafe { Transmute { from: PTR }.into };
[275](https://docs.rs#275)//!    ```
[276](https://docs.rs#276)//!
[277](https://docs.rs#277)//!    Finally, we can dereference our bytes:
[278](https://docs.rs#278)//!
[279](https://docs.rs#279)//!    ```rust
[280](https://docs.rs#280)//!    # const N: usize = 0;
[281](https://docs.rs#281)//!    # const REF: &[u8; N] = &[];
[282](https://docs.rs#282)//!    #[used]
[283](https://docs.rs#283)//!    #[link_section = "__TEXT,__info_plist"]
[284](https://docs.rs#284)//!    static PLIST: [u8; N] = *REF;
[285](https://docs.rs#285)//!    ```
[286](https://docs.rs#286)//!

[318](https://docs.rs#318)// This exists to ensure there are no conflicts when calling `include_bytes!`.
[319](https://docs.rs#319)// It is not part of this crate's public API, so I reserve the right to change
[320](https://docs.rs#320)// or remove this in a SemVer-compatible update.
[321](https://docs.rs#321)#[doc(hidden)]
[322](https://docs.rs#322)pub use core as _core;
[323](https://docs.rs#323)
[324](https://docs.rs#324)/// Embeds the [`Info.plist`] file at `$path` directly in the current binary.
[325](https://docs.rs#325)///
[326](https://docs.rs#326)/// After using this macro, you can get its content by calling
[327](https://docs.rs#327)/// [`get_info_plist`] from anywhere in your program.
[328](https://docs.rs#328)///
[329](https://docs.rs#329)/// # Accidental Reuse Protection
[330](https://docs.rs#330)///
[331](https://docs.rs#331)/// Only one copy of `Info.plist` should exist in a binary. Accidentally embedding
[332](https://docs.rs#332)/// it multiple times would break tools that read this section.
[333](https://docs.rs#333)///
[334](https://docs.rs#334)/// Fortunately, this library makes reuse a compile-time error! This protection
[335](https://docs.rs#335)/// works even if this macro is reused in different modules.
[336](https://docs.rs#336)///
[337](https://docs.rs#337)/// ```compile_fail
[338](https://docs.rs#338)/// # #[cfg(pass_reuse_doctest)]
[339](https://docs.rs#339)/// # compile_error!("hack to force a doctest compile error pre 1.43");
[340](https://docs.rs#340)/// embed_plist::embed_info_plist!("Info.plist");
[341](https://docs.rs#341)/// embed_plist::embed_info_plist!("Info.plist");
[342](https://docs.rs#342)/// ```
[343](https://docs.rs#343)///
[344](https://docs.rs#344)/// This example produces the following error:
[345](https://docs.rs#345)///
[346](https://docs.rs#346)/// ```text
[347](https://docs.rs#347)/// error: symbol `_EMBED_INFO_PLIST` is already defined
[348](https://docs.rs#348)///  --> src/main.rs:4:1
[349](https://docs.rs#349)///   |
[350](https://docs.rs#350)/// 4 | embed_plist::embed_info_plist!("Info.plist");
[351](https://docs.rs#351)///   | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
[352](https://docs.rs#352)///   |
[353](https://docs.rs#353)///   = note: this error originates in a macro (in Nightly builds, run with -Z macro-backtrace for more info)
[354](https://docs.rs#354)///
[355](https://docs.rs#355)/// error: aborting due to previous error
[356](https://docs.rs#356)/// ```
[357](https://docs.rs#357)///
[358](https://docs.rs#358)/// <p style="background:rgba(255, 181, 77, 0.16);padding:0.75em;">
[359](https://docs.rs#359)/// <b>Warning:</b> Although the name
[360](https://docs.rs#360)/// <code style="background:rgba(41, 24, 0, 0.1);">_EMBED_INFO_PLIST</code>
[361](https://docs.rs#361)/// can be seen here, you <strong>should not</strong> reference this symbol with
[362](https://docs.rs#362)/// e.g. an
[363](https://docs.rs#363)/// <code style="background:rgba(41, 24, 0, 0.1);">extern "C"</code>
[364](https://docs.rs#364)/// block. I reserve the right to change this name in a SemVer-compatible
[365](https://docs.rs#365)/// update.
[366](https://docs.rs#366)/// </p>
[367](https://docs.rs#367)///
[368](https://docs.rs#368)/// [`get_info_plist`]: fn.get_info_plist.html
[369](https://docs.rs#369)/// [`Info.plist`]: https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/General/Reference/InfoPlistKeyReference/Introduction/Introduction.html
[370](https://docs.rs#370)#[macro_export]
[371](https://docs.rs#371)macro_rules! embed_info_plist {
[372](https://docs.rs#372)    ($path:expr) => {
[373](https://docs.rs#373)        $crate::embed_info_plist_bytes!($crate::_core::include_bytes!($path));
[374](https://docs.rs#374)    };
[375](https://docs.rs#375)}
[376](https://docs.rs#376)
[377](https://docs.rs#377)/// Embeds the [`Info.plist`] file in `&[u8]` directly in the current binary.
[378](https://docs.rs#378)///
[379](https://docs.rs#379)/// This enables you to have more control over what bytes are embedded into your
[380](https://docs.rs#380)/// program. For example, you may want to do `const`-compatible preprocessing
[381](https://docs.rs#381)/// such as converting into a binary property list.
[382](https://docs.rs#382)///
[383](https://docs.rs#383)/// The [`embed_info_plist!`] macro is a convenience wrapper around this and
[384](https://docs.rs#384)/// [`include_bytes!`].
[385](https://docs.rs#385)///
[386](https://docs.rs#386)/// # Examples
[387](https://docs.rs#387)///
[388](https://docs.rs#388)/// After using this macro, you can get its content by calling
[389](https://docs.rs#389)/// [`get_info_plist`] from anywhere in your program:
[390](https://docs.rs#390)///
[391](https://docs.rs#391)/// ```rust
[392](https://docs.rs#392)/// const PLIST: &[u8] = r#"
[393](https://docs.rs#393)///     <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
[394](https://docs.rs#394)///     <!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
[395](https://docs.rs#395)///     <plist version="1.0">
[396](https://docs.rs#396)///     <dict>
[397](https://docs.rs#397)///         <key>Why</key>
[398](https://docs.rs#398)///         <string>To use in doc tests</string>
[399](https://docs.rs#399)///     </dict>
[400](https://docs.rs#400)///     </plist>
[401](https://docs.rs#401)/// "#.as_bytes();
[402](https://docs.rs#402)///
[403](https://docs.rs#403)/// embed_plist::embed_info_plist_bytes!(PLIST);
[404](https://docs.rs#404)/// let embedded = embed_plist::get_info_plist();
[405](https://docs.rs#405)///
[406](https://docs.rs#406)/// assert_eq!(embedded, PLIST);
[407](https://docs.rs#407)/// ```
[408](https://docs.rs#408)///
[409](https://docs.rs#409)/// [`get_info_plist`]: fn.get_info_plist.html
[410](https://docs.rs#410)/// [`embed_info_plist!`]: macro.embed_info_plist.html
[411](https://docs.rs#411)///
[412](https://docs.rs#412)/// [`Info.plist`]: https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/General/Reference/InfoPlistKeyReference/Introduction/Introduction.html
[413](https://docs.rs#413)/// [`include_bytes!`]: https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/macro.include_bytes.html
[414](https://docs.rs#414)#[macro_export]
[415](https://docs.rs#415)macro_rules! embed_info_plist_bytes {
[416](https://docs.rs#416)    ($bytes:expr) => {
[417](https://docs.rs#417)        // The wildcard `_` prevents polluting the call site with identifiers.
[418](https://docs.rs#418)        const _: () = {
[419](https://docs.rs#419)            // Because `len` is a `const fn`, we can use it to turn `SLICE` into
[420](https://docs.rs#420)            // an array that gets directly embedded. This is necessary because
[421](https://docs.rs#421)            // the `__info_plist` section must contain the direct data, not a
[422](https://docs.rs#422)            // reference to it.
[423](https://docs.rs#423)            const SLICE: &[u8] = $bytes;
[424](https://docs.rs#424)            const LEN: usize = SLICE.len();
[425](https://docs.rs#425)
[426](https://docs.rs#426)            union Transmute {
[427](https://docs.rs#427)                from: *const [u8; LEN],
[428](https://docs.rs#428)                into: &'static [u8; LEN],
[429](https://docs.rs#429)            }
[430](https://docs.rs#430)
[431](https://docs.rs#431)            const PTR: *const [u8; LEN] = SLICE.as_ptr() as *const _;
[432](https://docs.rs#432)            const REF: &[u8; LEN] = unsafe { Transmute { from: PTR }.into };
[433](https://docs.rs#433)
[434](https://docs.rs#434)            // Prevents this from being optimized out of the binary.
[435](https://docs.rs#435)            #[used]
[436](https://docs.rs#436)            // Places this data in the correct location.
[437](https://docs.rs#437)            #[link_section = "__TEXT,__info_plist,regular,no_dead_strip"]
[438](https://docs.rs#438)            // Prevents repeated use by creating a linker error.
[439](https://docs.rs#439)            #[no_mangle]
[440](https://docs.rs#440)            pub static _EMBED_INFO_PLIST: [u8; LEN] = *REF;
[441](https://docs.rs#441)        };
[442](https://docs.rs#442)    };
[443](https://docs.rs#443)}
[444](https://docs.rs#444)
[445](https://docs.rs#445)/// Embeds the [`launchd.plist`] file at `$path` directly in the current binary.
[446](https://docs.rs#446)///
[447](https://docs.rs#447)/// After using this macro, you can get its content by calling
[448](https://docs.rs#448)/// [`get_launchd_plist`] from anywhere in your program.
[449](https://docs.rs#449)///
[450](https://docs.rs#450)/// # Accidental Reuse Protection
[451](https://docs.rs#451)///
[452](https://docs.rs#452)/// Only one copy of `launchd.plist` should exist in a binary. Accidentally
[453](https://docs.rs#453)/// embedding it multiple times would break tools that read this section.
[454](https://docs.rs#454)///
[455](https://docs.rs#455)/// Fortunately, this library makes reuse a compile-time error! This protection
[456](https://docs.rs#456)/// works even if this macro is reused in different modules.
[457](https://docs.rs#457)///
[458](https://docs.rs#458)/// ```compile_fail
[459](https://docs.rs#459)/// # #[cfg(pass_reuse_doctest)]
[460](https://docs.rs#460)/// # compile_error!("hack to force a doctest compile error pre 1.43");
[461](https://docs.rs#461)/// embed_plist::embed_launchd_plist!("launchd.plist");
[462](https://docs.rs#462)/// embed_plist::embed_launchd_plist!("launchd.plist");
[463](https://docs.rs#463)/// ```
[464](https://docs.rs#464)///
[465](https://docs.rs#465)/// This example produces the following error:
[466](https://docs.rs#466)///
[467](https://docs.rs#467)/// ```txt
[468](https://docs.rs#468)/// error: symbol `_EMBED_LAUNCHD_PLIST` is already defined
[469](https://docs.rs#469)///  --> src/main.rs:4:1
[470](https://docs.rs#470)///   |
[471](https://docs.rs#471)/// 4 | embed_plist::embed_launchd_plist!("launchd.plist");
[472](https://docs.rs#472)///   | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
[473](https://docs.rs#473)///   |
[474](https://docs.rs#474)///   = note: this error originates in a macro (in Nightly builds, run with -Z macro-backtrace for more info)
[475](https://docs.rs#475)///
[476](https://docs.rs#476)/// error: aborting due to previous error
[477](https://docs.rs#477)/// ```
[478](https://docs.rs#478)///
[479](https://docs.rs#479)/// <p style="background:rgba(255, 181, 77, 0.16);padding:0.75em;">
[480](https://docs.rs#480)/// <b>Warning:</b> Although the name
[481](https://docs.rs#481)/// <code style="background:rgba(41, 24, 0, 0.1);">_EMBED_LAUNCHD_PLIST</code>
[482](https://docs.rs#482)/// can be seen here, you <strong>should not</strong> reference this symbol with
[483](https://docs.rs#483)/// e.g. an
[484](https://docs.rs#484)/// <code style="background:rgba(41, 24, 0, 0.1);">extern "C"</code>
[485](https://docs.rs#485)/// block. I reserve the right to change this name in a SemVer-compatible
[486](https://docs.rs#486)/// update.
[487](https://docs.rs#487)/// </p>
[488](https://docs.rs#488)///
[489](https://docs.rs#489)/// [`get_launchd_plist`]: fn.get_launchd_plist.html
[490](https://docs.rs#490)/// [`launchd.plist`]: https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/MacOSX/Conceptual/BPSystemStartup/Chapters/CreatingLaunchdJobs.html#//apple_ref/doc/uid/TP40001762-104142
[491](https://docs.rs#491)#[macro_export]
[492](https://docs.rs#492)macro_rules! embed_launchd_plist {
[493](https://docs.rs#493)    ($path:expr) => {
[494](https://docs.rs#494)        $crate::embed_launchd_plist_bytes!($crate::_core::include_bytes!(
[495](https://docs.rs#495)            $path
[496](https://docs.rs#496)        ));
[497](https://docs.rs#497)    };
[498](https://docs.rs#498)}
[499](https://docs.rs#499)
[500](https://docs.rs#500)/// Embeds the [`launchd.plist`] file in `&[u8]` directly in the current binary.
[501](https://docs.rs#501)///
[502](https://docs.rs#502)/// This enables you to have more control over what bytes are embedded into your
[503](https://docs.rs#503)/// program. For example, you may want to do `const`-compatible preprocessing
[504](https://docs.rs#504)/// such as converting into a binary property list.
[505](https://docs.rs#505)///
[506](https://docs.rs#506)/// The [`embed_launchd_plist!`] macro is a convenience wrapper around this and
[507](https://docs.rs#507)/// [`include_bytes!`].
[508](https://docs.rs#508)///
[509](https://docs.rs#509)/// # Examples
[510](https://docs.rs#510)///
[511](https://docs.rs#511)/// After using this macro, you can get its content by calling
[512](https://docs.rs#512)/// [`get_launchd_plist`] from anywhere in your program:
[513](https://docs.rs#513)///
[514](https://docs.rs#514)/// ```rust
[515](https://docs.rs#515)/// const PLIST: &[u8] = r#"
[516](https://docs.rs#516)///     <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
[517](https://docs.rs#517)///     <!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
[518](https://docs.rs#518)///     <plist version="1.0">
[519](https://docs.rs#519)///     <dict>
[520](https://docs.rs#520)///         <key>Why</key>
[521](https://docs.rs#521)///         <string>To use in doc tests</string>
[522](https://docs.rs#522)///         <key>Label</key>
[523](https://docs.rs#523)///         <string>example</string>
[524](https://docs.rs#524)///         <key>ProgramArguments</key>
[525](https://docs.rs#525)///         <array>
[526](https://docs.rs#526)///             <string>Hello</string>
[527](https://docs.rs#527)///             <string>World</string>
[528](https://docs.rs#528)///         </array>
[529](https://docs.rs#529)///     </dict>
[530](https://docs.rs#530)///     </plist>
[531](https://docs.rs#531)/// "#.as_bytes();
[532](https://docs.rs#532)///
[533](https://docs.rs#533)/// embed_plist::embed_launchd_plist_bytes!(PLIST);
[534](https://docs.rs#534)/// let embedded = embed_plist::get_launchd_plist();
[535](https://docs.rs#535)///
[536](https://docs.rs#536)/// assert_eq!(embedded, PLIST);
[537](https://docs.rs#537)/// ```
[538](https://docs.rs#538)///
[539](https://docs.rs#539)/// [`get_launchd_plist`]: fn.get_launchd_plist.html
[540](https://docs.rs#540)/// [`embed_launchd_plist!`]: macro.embed_launchd_plist.html
[541](https://docs.rs#541)///
[542](https://docs.rs#542)/// [`launchd.plist`]: https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/MacOSX/Conceptual/BPSystemStartup/Chapters/CreatingLaunchdJobs.html#//apple_ref/doc/uid/TP40001762-104142
[543](https://docs.rs#543)/// [`include_bytes!`]: https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/macro.include_bytes.html
[544](https://docs.rs#544)#[macro_export]
[545](https://docs.rs#545)macro_rules! embed_launchd_plist_bytes {
[546](https://docs.rs#546)    ($bytes:expr) => {
[547](https://docs.rs#547)        // The wildcard `_` prevents polluting the call site with identifiers.
[548](https://docs.rs#548)        const _: () = {
[549](https://docs.rs#549)            // Because `len` is a `const fn`, we can use it to turn `SLICE` into
[550](https://docs.rs#550)            // an array that gets directly embedded. This is necessary because
[551](https://docs.rs#551)            // the `__launchd_plist` section must contain the direct data, not a
[552](https://docs.rs#552)            // reference to it.
[553](https://docs.rs#553)            const SLICE: &[u8] = $bytes;
[554](https://docs.rs#554)            const LEN: usize = SLICE.len();
[555](https://docs.rs#555)
[556](https://docs.rs#556)            union Transmute {
[557](https://docs.rs#557)                from: *const [u8; LEN],
[558](https://docs.rs#558)                into: &'static [u8; LEN],
[559](https://docs.rs#559)            }
[560](https://docs.rs#560)
[561](https://docs.rs#561)            const PTR: *const [u8; LEN] = SLICE.as_ptr() as *const _;
[562](https://docs.rs#562)            const REF: &[u8; LEN] = unsafe { Transmute { from: PTR }.into };
[563](https://docs.rs#563)
[564](https://docs.rs#564)            // Prevents this from being optimized out of the binary.
[565](https://docs.rs#565)            #[used]
[566](https://docs.rs#566)            // Places this data in the correct location.
[567](https://docs.rs#567)            #[link_section = "__TEXT,__launchd_plist,regular,no_dead_strip"]
[568](https://docs.rs#568)            // Prevents repeated use by creating a linker error.
[569](https://docs.rs#569)            #[no_mangle]
[570](https://docs.rs#570)            pub static _EMBED_LAUNCHD_PLIST: [u8; LEN] = *REF;
[571](https://docs.rs#571)        };
[572](https://docs.rs#572)    };
[573](https://docs.rs#573)}
[574](https://docs.rs#574)
[575](https://docs.rs#575)/// Returns the contents of the embedded [`Info.plist`] file.
[576](https://docs.rs#576)///
[577](https://docs.rs#577)/// # Examples
[578](https://docs.rs#578)///
[579](https://docs.rs#579)/// We can verify that the result is correct by checking it against the file at
[580](https://docs.rs#580)/// runtime:
[581](https://docs.rs#581)///
[582](https://docs.rs#582)/// ```rust
[583](https://docs.rs#583)/// # fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
[584](https://docs.rs#584)/// # std::env::set_current_dir("./src")?;
[585](https://docs.rs#585)/// embed_plist::embed_info_plist!("Info.plist");
[586](https://docs.rs#586)///
[587](https://docs.rs#587)/// let embedded_plist = embed_plist::get_info_plist();
[588](https://docs.rs#588)/// let read_plist = std::fs::read("Info.plist")?;
[589](https://docs.rs#589)///
[590](https://docs.rs#590)/// assert_eq!(embedded_plist, read_plist.as_slice());
[591](https://docs.rs#591)/// # Ok(())
[592](https://docs.rs#592)/// # }
[593](https://docs.rs#593)/// ```
[594](https://docs.rs#594)///
[595](https://docs.rs#595)/// If `embed_info_plist!` has not been called, this function creates a
[596](https://docs.rs#596)/// compile-time error by failing to reference the symbol defined by that macro:
[597](https://docs.rs#597)///
[598](https://docs.rs#598)/// ```compile_fail
[599](https://docs.rs#599)/// # #[cfg(pass_reuse_doctest)]
[600](https://docs.rs#600)/// # compile_error!("hack to force a doctest compile error pre 1.43");
[601](https://docs.rs#601)/// let embedded_plist = embed_plist::get_info_plist();
[602](https://docs.rs#602)/// ```
[603](https://docs.rs#603)///
[604](https://docs.rs#604)/// # Safety
[605](https://docs.rs#605)///
[606](https://docs.rs#606)/// This function relies on `_EMBED_INFO_PLIST` being defined within the
[607](https://docs.rs#607)/// `__TEXT,__info_plist` section. You **should not** define this symbol outside
[608](https://docs.rs#608)/// of using the macros provided by this library.
[609](https://docs.rs#609)///
[610](https://docs.rs#610)/// [`Info.plist`]: https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/General/Reference/InfoPlistKeyReference/Introduction/Introduction.html
[611](https://docs.rs#611)#[inline]
[612](https://docs.rs#612)pub fn get_info_plist() -> &'static [u8] {
[613](https://docs.rs#613)    extern "C" {
[614](https://docs.rs#614)        // Using this symbol instead of section start to force a linker error if
[615](https://docs.rs#615)        // `embed_info_plist!` has not been called.
[616](https://docs.rs#616)        #[link_name = "_EMBED_INFO_PLIST"]
[617](https://docs.rs#617)        static START: [u8; 0];
[618](https://docs.rs#618)
[619](https://docs.rs#619)        #[link_name = "\x01section$end$__TEXT$__info_plist"]
[620](https://docs.rs#620)        static END: [u8; 0];
[621](https://docs.rs#621)    }
[622](https://docs.rs#622)    unsafe {
[623](https://docs.rs#623)        let start = START.as_ptr();
[624](https://docs.rs#624)        let end = END.as_ptr();
[625](https://docs.rs#625)        let len = end as usize - start as usize;
[626](https://docs.rs#626)        core::slice::from_raw_parts(start, len)
[627](https://docs.rs#627)    }
[628](https://docs.rs#628)}
[629](https://docs.rs#629)
[630](https://docs.rs#630)/// Returns the contents of the embedded [`launchd.plist`] file.
[631](https://docs.rs#631)///

[636](https://docs.rs#636)///

[641](https://docs.rs#641)///

[644](https://docs.rs#644)///

[646](https://docs.rs#646)/// # Ok(())
[647](https://docs.rs#647)/// # }
[648](https://docs.rs#648)/// ```

[651](https://docs.rs#651)/// compile-time error by failing to reference the symbol defined by that macro:
[652](https://docs.rs#652)///

[664](https://docs.rs#664)///
[665](https://docs.rs#665)/// [`embed_launchd_plist!`]: macro.embed_launchd_plist.html
[666](https://docs.rs#666)/// [`launchd.plist`]: https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/MacOSX/Conceptual/BPSystemStartup/Chapters/CreatingLaunchdJobs.html#//apple_ref/doc/uid/TP40001762-104142
[667](https://docs.rs#667)#[inline]
[668](https://docs.rs#668)pub fn get_launchd_plist() -> &'static [u8] {
[669](https://docs.rs#669)    extern "C" {
[670](https://docs.rs#670)        // Using this symbol instead of section start to force a linker error if
[671](https://docs.rs#671)        // `embed_launchd_plist!` has not been called.
[672](https://docs.rs#672)        #[link_name = "_EMBED_LAUNCHD_PLIST"]

# get_info_plist in embed_plist - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/embed_plist/1.2.2/embed_plist/fn.get_info_plist.html

`pub fn get_info_plist() -> &'static [`[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u8.html)]## Expand description

Returns the contents of the embedded [ Info.plist](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/General/Reference/InfoPlistKeyReference/Introduction/Introduction.html) file.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

We can verify that the result is correct by checking it against the file at runtime:

```
embed_plist::embed_info_plist!("Info.plist");
let embedded_plist = embed_plist::get_info_plist();
let read_plist = std::fs::read("Info.plist")?;
assert_eq!(embedded_plist, read_plist.as_slice());
```
If `embed_info_plist!` has not been called, this function creates a
compile-time error by failing to reference the symbol defined by that macro:

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

This function relies on `_EMBED_INFO_PLIST` being defined within the
`__TEXT,__info_plist` section. You **should not** define this symbol outside
of using the macros provided by this library.

# embed_info_plist in embed_plist - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/embed_plist/1.2.2/embed_plist/macro.embed_info_plist.html

```
macro_rules! embed_info_plist {
    ($path:expr) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Embeds the [ Info.plist](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/General/Reference/InfoPlistKeyReference/Introduction/Introduction.html) file at

`$path` directly in the current binary.After using this macro, you can get its content by calling
[ get_info_plist](https://docs.rs/fn.get_info_plist.html) from anywhere in your program.

[§](https://docs.rs#accidental-reuse-protection)Accidental Reuse Protection

Only one copy of `Info.plist` should exist in a binary. Accidentally embedding
it multiple times would break tools that read this section.

Fortunately, this library makes reuse a compile-time error! This protection works even if this macro is reused in different modules.

This example produces the following error:

```
error: symbol `_EMBED_INFO_PLIST` is already defined
 --> src/main.rs:4:1
  |
4 | embed_plist::embed_info_plist!("Info.plist");
  | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  |
  = note: this error originates in a macro (in Nightly builds, run with -Z macro-backtrace for more info)
error: aborting due to previous error
```
**Warning:** Although the name
`_EMBED_INFO_PLIST`
can be seen here, you **should not** reference this symbol with
e.g. an
`extern "C"`
block. I reserve the right to change this name in a SemVer-compatible
update.

# embed_launchd_plist_bytes in embed_plist - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/embed_plist/1.2.2/embed_plist/macro.embed_launchd_plist_bytes.html

```
macro_rules! embed_launchd_plist_bytes {
    ($bytes:expr) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Embeds the [ launchd.plist](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/MacOSX/Conceptual/BPSystemStartup/Chapters/CreatingLaunchdJobs.html#//apple_ref/doc/uid/TP40001762-104142) file in

`&[u8]` directly in the current binary.This enables you to have more control over what bytes are embedded into your
program. For example, you may want to do `const`-compatible preprocessing
such as converting into a binary property list.

The [ embed_launchd_plist!](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_launchd_plist.html) macro is a convenience wrapper around this and

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/macro.include_bytes.html)

`include_bytes!`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

After using this macro, you can get its content by calling
[ get_launchd_plist](https://docs.rs/fn.get_launchd_plist.html) from anywhere in your program:

```
const PLIST: &[u8] = r#"
    <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
    <!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
    <plist version="1.0">
    <dict>
        <key>Why</key>
        <string>To use in doc tests</string>
        <key>Label</key>
        <string>example</string>
        <key>ProgramArguments</key>
        <array>
            <string>Hello</string>
            <string>World</string>
        </array>
    </dict>
    </plist>
"#.as_bytes();
embed_plist::embed_launchd_plist_bytes!(PLIST);
let embedded = embed_plist::get_launchd_plist();
assert_eq!(embedded, PLIST);
```

# embed_plist - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/embed_plist/latest/embed_plist/

## Expand description

Embed an [ Info.plist](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/General/Reference/InfoPlistKeyReference/Introduction/Introduction.html) or

[file directly in your executable binary, brought to you by](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/MacOSX/Conceptual/BPSystemStartup/Chapters/CreatingLaunchdJobs.html#//apple_ref/doc/uid/TP40001762-104142)

`launchd.plist`[@NikolaiVazquez](https://twitter.com/NikolaiVazquez)!

If you found this library useful, please consider
[sponsoring me on GitHub](https://github.com/sponsors/nvzqz). ❤️

[§](https://docs.rs#index)Index

- [Motivation](https://docs.rs#motivation)
- [Usage](https://docs.rs#usage)
- [Minimum Supported Rust Version](https://docs.rs#minimum-supported-rust-version)
- [Multi-Target Considerations](https://docs.rs#multi-target-considerations)
- [Get Embedded Property Lists](https://docs.rs#get-embedded-property-lists)
- [Accidental Reuse Protection](https://docs.rs#accidental-reuse-protection)
- [Implementation](https://docs.rs#implementation)
- [License](https://docs.rs#license)
- [Macros](https://docs.rs#macros)
- [Functions](https://docs.rs#functions)

[§](https://docs.rs#motivation)Motivation

Certain programs require an embedded `Info.plist` or `launchd.plist` file to
work correctly. For example:

-
`Info.plist`is needed to obtain certain permissions on macOS 10.15 and later.
-
`launchd.plist`is needed to make`launchd`daemons and user agents

Doing this manually with [ include_bytes!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/macro.include_bytes.html) is cumbersome. To understand
why, see the

[implementation](https://docs.rs#implementation). This library removes the headache of doing this.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

This library is available [on crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/embed_plist) and can be used by adding
the following to your project’s [ Cargo.toml](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html):

```
[dependencies]
embed_plist = "1.2"
```
…and this to any source file in your crate:

```
embed_plist::embed_info_plist!("Info.plist");
// If making a daemon:
embed_plist::embed_launchd_plist!("launchd.plist");
```
Done! It’s that simple. 🙂

See [implementation](https://docs.rs#implementation) for details on this sorcery.

[§](https://docs.rs#minimum-supported-rust-version)Minimum Supported Rust Version

This library targets **1.39** as its minimum supported Rust version
(MSRV).

Requiring a newer Rust version is considered a breaking change and will
result in a “major” library version update. In other words: `0.1.z` would
become `0.2.0`, or `1.y.z` would become `2.0.0`.

[§](https://docs.rs#multi-target-considerations)Multi-Target Considerations

This library only works for [Mach-O](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mach-O)
binaries. When building a cross-platform program, these macro calls should
be placed behind a `#[cfg]` to prevent linker errors on other targets.

```
#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
embed_plist::embed_info_plist!("Info.plist");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#get-embedded-property-lists)Get Embedded Property Lists

After using these macros, you can get their contents by calling
[ get_info_plist](https://docs.rs/fn.get_info_plist.html) or

[from anywhere in your program.](https://docs.rs/fn.get_launchd_plist.html)

`get_launchd_plist`We can verify that the result is correct by checking it against reading the appropriate file at runtime:

```
embed_plist::embed_info_plist!("Info.plist");
let embedded_plist = embed_plist::get_info_plist();
let read_plist = std::fs::read("Info.plist")?;
assert_eq!(embedded_plist, read_plist.as_slice());
```
If the appropriate macro has not been called, each function creates a compile-time error by failing to reference the symbol defined by that macro:

[§](https://docs.rs#accidental-reuse-protection)Accidental Reuse Protection

Only one copy of `Info.plist` or `launchd.plist` should exist in a binary.
Accidentally embedding them multiple times would break tools that read these
sections.

Fortunately, this library makes reuse a compile-time error! This protection works even if these macros are reused in different modules.

This example produces the following error:

```
error: symbol `_EMBED_INFO_PLIST` is already defined
 --> src/main.rs:4:1
  |
4 | embed_plist::embed_info_plist!("Info.plist");
  | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  |
  = note: this error originates in a macro (in Nightly builds, run with -Z macro-backtrace for more info)
error: aborting due to previous error
```
**Warning:** Although the name
`_EMBED_INFO_PLIST`
can be seen here, you **should not** reference this symbol with
e.g. an
`extern "C"`
block. I reserve the right to change this name in a SemVer-compatible
update.

[§](https://docs.rs#implementation)Implementation

Files are read using [ include_bytes!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/macro.include_bytes.html). This normally places data in

`__TEXT,__const`, where immutable data is kept. However, property list data
is expected to be in `__TEXT,__info_plist` or `__TEXT,__launchd_plist`. This
section will explain how I accomplish that.We begin by reading the file from disk:

`const BYTES: &[u8] = include_bytes!("Info.plist");`A naïve approach is to do the following:

```
#[used] // Prevent optimizing out
#[link_section = "__TEXT,__info_plist"]
static PLIST: &[u8] = BYTES;
```
This doesn’t work because only the slice’s pointer and length that are
placed in `__TEXT,__info_plist`. The referenced bytes are still placed in
`__TEXT,__const`.

Instead, we need to arrive at the following:

```
#[used]
#[link_section = "__TEXT,__info_plist"]
static PLIST: [u8; N] = *BYTES;
```
We can get `N` by using [ len](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.slice.html#method.len). As of Rust 1.39, it is possible to get the
length of a slice within a

`const`.`const N: usize = BYTES.len();`The next step is to dereference the bytes into a `[u8; N]`.

There are two approaches:

-
`include_bytes!`This is not the approach used by this library because of concerns about compile performance. See the [second approach](https://docs.rs#approach-2)for what this library does.The following is all we need: `#[used] #[link_section = "__TEXT,__info_plist"] static PLIST: [u8; N] = *include_bytes!("Info.plist");`This works because `include_bytes!`actually returns a`&[u8; N]`. It’s often used as a`&[u8]`because we don’t know the size when calling it.
-
This is tricker than the [first approach](https://docs.rs#approach-1)(and somewhat cursed). If you know me, then it’s predictable I’d go this route.We can get a pointer to the bytes via `as_ptr``const`:`const PTR: *const [u8; N] = BYTES.as_ptr() as *const [u8; N];`Unfortunately, this pointer can’t be directly dereferenced in Rust 1.39 (minimum supported version). Instead, we must cast the pointer to a reference. You may want to reach for `transmute``const`in Rust 1.46. However, earlier versions need to be supported, so that is not an option for this library.This bitwise cast can be accomplished with a `union`:`union Transmute { from: *const [u8; N], into: &'static [u8; N], } const REF: &[u8; N] = unsafe { Transmute { from: PTR }.into };`Finally, we can dereference our bytes: `#[used] #[link_section = "__TEXT,__info_plist"] static PLIST: [u8; N] = *REF;`

[§](https://docs.rs#license)License

This project is released under either:

at your choosing.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [embed_](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_info_plist.html)- info_ - plist
- Embeds the `Info.plist``$path`directly in the current binary.
- [embed_](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_info_plist_bytes.html)- info_ - plist_ - bytes
- Embeds the `Info.plist``&[u8]`directly in the current binary.
- [embed_](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_launchd_plist.html)- launchd_ - plist
- Embeds the `launchd.plist``$path`directly in the current binary.
- [embed_](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_launchd_plist_bytes.html)- launchd_ - plist_ - bytes
- Embeds the `launchd.plist``&[u8]`directly in the current binary.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [get_](https://docs.rs/fn.get_info_plist.html)- info_ - plist
- Returns the contents of the embedded `Info.plist`
- [get_](https://docs.rs/fn.get_launchd_plist.html)- launchd_ - plist
- Returns the contents of the embedded `launchd.plist`

---

# embed_plist 1.2.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/embed_plist/latest/builds

All the builds on docs.rs are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The limits for this crate are the following:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                    If a build fails because it hit one of those limits please
                    [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                    to get them increased.

# embed_plist 1.2.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/embed_plist/1.2.1

Embed an [ Info.plist](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/General/Reference/InfoPlistKeyReference/Introduction/Introduction.html) or

[file directly in your executable binary, brought to you by](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/MacOSX/Conceptual/BPSystemStartup/Chapters/CreatingLaunchdJobs.html#//apple_ref/doc/uid/TP40001762-104142)

`launchd.plist`[@NikolaiVazquez](https://twitter.com/NikolaiVazquez)!

If you found this library useful, please consider
[sponsoring me on GitHub](https://github.com/sponsors/nvzqz). ❤️

## Index

- [Motivation](https://docs.rs#motivation)
- [Usage](https://docs.rs#usage)
- [Minimum Supported Rust Version](https://docs.rs#minimum-supported-rust-version)
- [Multi-Target Considerations](https://docs.rs#multi-target-considerations)
- [Get Embedded Property Lists](https://docs.rs#get-embedded-property-lists)
- [Accidental Reuse Protection](https://docs.rs#accidental-reuse-protection)
- [Implementation](https://docs.rs#implementation)
- [License](https://docs.rs#license)

## Motivation

Certain programs require an embedded `Info.plist` or `launchd.plist` file to
work correctly. For example:

-
`Info.plist`is needed to obtain certain permissions on macOS 10.15 and later.
-
`launchd.plist`is needed to make`launchd`daemons and user agents

Doing this manually with [ include_bytes!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/macro.include_bytes.html) is cumbersome. To understand
why, see the

[implementation](https://docs.rs#implementation). This library removes the headache of doing this.

## Usage

This library is available [on crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/embed_plist) and can be used by adding
the following to your project's [ Cargo.toml](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html):

```
[]
 = "1.2"
```
...and this to any source file in your crate:

```
embed_info_plist!;
// If making a daemon:
embed_launchd_plist!;
```
Done! It's that simple. 🙂

See [implementation](https://docs.rs#implementation) for details on this sorcery.

## Minimum Supported Rust Version

This library targets 1.39 as its minimum supported Rust version (MSRV).

Requiring a newer Rust version is considered a breaking change and will
result in a "major" library version update. In other words: `0.1.z` would
become `0.2.0`, or `1.y.z` would become `2.0.0`.

## Multi-Target Considerations

This library only works for [Mach-O](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mach-O)
binaries. When building a cross-platform program, these macro calls should
be placed behind a `#[cfg]` to prevent linker errors on other targets.

```
embed_info_plist!;
```
## Get Embedded Property Lists

After using these macros, you can get their contents by calling
[ get_info_plist](https://docs.rs/embed_plist/1.2.1/embed_plist/fn.get_info_plist.html) or

[from anywhere in your program.](https://docs.rs/embed_plist/1.2.1/embed_plist/fn.get_launchd_plist.html)

`get_launchd_plist`We can verify that the result is correct by checking it against reading the appropriate file at runtime:

```
embed_info_plist!;
let embedded_plist = get_info_plist;
let read_plist = read?;
assert_eq!;
```
If the appropriate macro has not been called, each function creates a compile-time error by failing to reference the symbol defined by that macro:

```
// This fails to compile:
let embedded_plist = get_info_plist;
```
## Accidental Reuse Protection

Only one copy of `Info.plist` or `launchd.plist` should exist in a binary.
Accidentally embedding them multiple times would break tools that read these
sections.

Fortunately, this library makes reuse a compile-time error! This protection works even if these macros are reused in different modules.

```
// This fails to compile:
embed_info_plist!;
embed_info_plist!;
```
This example produces the following error:

```
error: symbol `_EMBED_INFO_PLIST` is already defined
 --> src/main.rs:4:1
  |
4 | embed_plist::embed_info_plist!("Info.plist");
  | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  |
  = note: this error originates in a macro (in Nightly builds, run with -Z macro-backtrace for more info)
error: aborting due to previous error
```
Warning: Although the name

`_EMBED_INFO_PLIST`can be seen here, youshould notreference this symbol with e.g. an`extern "C"`block. I reserve the right to change this name in a SemVer-compatible update.

## Implementation

Files are read using [ include_bytes!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/macro.include_bytes.html). This normally places data in

`__TEXT,__const`, where immutable data is kept. However, property list data
is expected to be in `__TEXT,__info_plist` or `__TEXT,__launchd_plist`. This
section will explain how I accomplish that.We begin by reading the file from disk:

```
const BYTES: & = include_bytes!;
```
A naïve approach is to do the following:

```
 // Prevent optimizing out
static PLIST: & = BYTES;
```
This doesn't work because only the slice's pointer and length that are
placed in `__TEXT,__info_plist`. The referenced bytes are still placed in
`__TEXT,__const`.

Instead, we need to arrive at the following:

```
static PLIST:  = *BYTES;
```
We can get `N` by using [ len](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.slice.html#method.len). As of Rust 1.39, it is possible to get the
length of a slice within a

`const`.```
const N: usize = BYTES.len;
```
The next step is to dereference the bytes into a `[u8; N]`.

There are two approaches:

-
Call `include_bytes!`This is not the approach used by this library because of concerns about compile performance. See the [second approach](https://docs.rs#approach-2)for what this library does.The following is all we need: `static PLIST: = *include_bytes!;`This works because `include_bytes!`actually returns a`&[u8; N]`. It's often used as a`&[u8]`because we don't know the size when calling it.
-
Dereference our current bytes through pointer casting. This is tricker than the [first approach](https://docs.rs#approach-1)(and somewhat cursed). If you know me, then it's predictable I'd go this route.We can get a pointer to the bytes via `as_ptr``const`:`const PTR: *const = BYTES.as_ptr as *const ;`Unfortunately, this pointer can't be directly dereferenced in Rust 1.39 (minimum supported version). `// This fails to compile: static PLIST: = unsafe ;`Instead, we must cast the pointer to a reference. You may want to reach for `transmute``const`in Rust 1.46. However, earlier versions need to be supported, so that is not an option for this library.This bitwise cast can be accomplished with a `union`:`union Transmute const REF: & = unsafe ;`Finally, we can dereference our bytes: `static PLIST: = *REF;`

## License

This project is released under either:

at your choosing.

-
Call `include_bytes!`This is not the approach used by this library because of concerns about compile performance. See the [second approach](https://docs.rs#approach-2)for what this library does.The following is all we need: `static PLIST: = *include_bytes!;`This works because `include_bytes!`actually returns a`&[u8; N]`. It's often used as a`&[u8]`because we don't know the size when calling it.
-
Dereference our current bytes through pointer casting. This is tricker than the [first approach](https://docs.rs#approach-1)(and somewhat cursed). If you know me, then it's predictable I'd go this route.We can get a pointer to the bytes via `as_ptr``const`:`const PTR: *const = BYTES.as_ptr as *const ;`Unfortunately, this pointer can't be directly dereferenced in Rust 1.39 (minimum supported version). `// This fails to compile: static PLIST: = unsafe ;`Instead, we must cast the pointer to a reference. You may want to reach for `transmute``const`in Rust 1.46. However, earlier versions need to be supported, so that is not an option for this library.This bitwise cast can be accomplished with a `union`:`union Transmute const REF: & = unsafe ;`Finally, we can dereference our bytes: `static PLIST: = *REF;`

## License

This project is released under either:

at your choosing.

# embed_plist - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/embed_plist/latest/target-redirect/embed_plist/index.html

## Expand description

Embed an [ Info.plist](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/General/Reference/InfoPlistKeyReference/Introduction/Introduction.html) or

[file directly in your executable binary, brought to you by](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/MacOSX/Conceptual/BPSystemStartup/Chapters/CreatingLaunchdJobs.html#//apple_ref/doc/uid/TP40001762-104142)

`launchd.plist`[@NikolaiVazquez](https://twitter.com/NikolaiVazquez)!

If you found this library useful, please consider
[sponsoring me on GitHub](https://github.com/sponsors/nvzqz). ❤️

[§](https://docs.rs#index)Index

- [Motivation](https://docs.rs#motivation)
- [Usage](https://docs.rs#usage)
- [Minimum Supported Rust Version](https://docs.rs#minimum-supported-rust-version)
- [Multi-Target Considerations](https://docs.rs#multi-target-considerations)
- [Get Embedded Property Lists](https://docs.rs#get-embedded-property-lists)
- [Accidental Reuse Protection](https://docs.rs#accidental-reuse-protection)
- [Implementation](https://docs.rs#implementation)
- [License](https://docs.rs#license)
- [Macros](https://docs.rs#macros)
- [Functions](https://docs.rs#functions)

[§](https://docs.rs#motivation)Motivation

Certain programs require an embedded `Info.plist` or `launchd.plist` file to
work correctly. For example:

-
`Info.plist`is needed to obtain certain permissions on macOS 10.15 and later.
-
`launchd.plist`is needed to make`launchd`daemons and user agents

Doing this manually with [ include_bytes!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/macro.include_bytes.html) is cumbersome. To understand
why, see the

[implementation](https://docs.rs#implementation). This library removes the headache of doing this.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

This library is available [on crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/embed_plist) and can be used by adding
the following to your project’s [ Cargo.toml](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html):

```
[dependencies]
embed_plist = "1.2"
```
…and this to any source file in your crate:

```
embed_plist::embed_info_plist!("Info.plist");
// If making a daemon:
embed_plist::embed_launchd_plist!("launchd.plist");
```
Done! It’s that simple. 🙂

See [implementation](https://docs.rs#implementation) for details on this sorcery.

[§](https://docs.rs#minimum-supported-rust-version)Minimum Supported Rust Version

This library targets **1.39** as its minimum supported Rust version
(MSRV).

Requiring a newer Rust version is considered a breaking change and will
result in a “major” library version update. In other words: `0.1.z` would
become `0.2.0`, or `1.y.z` would become `2.0.0`.

[§](https://docs.rs#multi-target-considerations)Multi-Target Considerations

This library only works for [Mach-O](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mach-O)
binaries. When building a cross-platform program, these macro calls should
be placed behind a `#[cfg]` to prevent linker errors on other targets.

```
#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
embed_plist::embed_info_plist!("Info.plist");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#get-embedded-property-lists)Get Embedded Property Lists

After using these macros, you can get their contents by calling
[ get_info_plist](https://docs.rs/fn.get_info_plist.html) or

[from anywhere in your program.](https://docs.rs/fn.get_launchd_plist.html)

`get_launchd_plist`We can verify that the result is correct by checking it against reading the appropriate file at runtime:

```
embed_plist::embed_info_plist!("Info.plist");
let embedded_plist = embed_plist::get_info_plist();
let read_plist = std::fs::read("Info.plist")?;
assert_eq!(embedded_plist, read_plist.as_slice());
```
If the appropriate macro has not been called, each function creates a compile-time error by failing to reference the symbol defined by that macro:

[§](https://docs.rs#accidental-reuse-protection)Accidental Reuse Protection

Only one copy of `Info.plist` or `launchd.plist` should exist in a binary.
Accidentally embedding them multiple times would break tools that read these
sections.

Fortunately, this library makes reuse a compile-time error! This protection works even if these macros are reused in different modules.

This example produces the following error:

```
error: symbol `_EMBED_INFO_PLIST` is already defined
 --> src/main.rs:4:1
  |
4 | embed_plist::embed_info_plist!("Info.plist");
  | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  |
  = note: this error originates in a macro (in Nightly builds, run with -Z macro-backtrace for more info)
error: aborting due to previous error
```
**Warning:** Although the name
`_EMBED_INFO_PLIST`
can be seen here, you **should not** reference this symbol with
e.g. an
`extern "C"`
block. I reserve the right to change this name in a SemVer-compatible
update.

[§](https://docs.rs#implementation)Implementation

Files are read using [ include_bytes!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/macro.include_bytes.html). This normally places data in

`__TEXT,__const`, where immutable data is kept. However, property list data
is expected to be in `__TEXT,__info_plist` or `__TEXT,__launchd_plist`. This
section will explain how I accomplish that.We begin by reading the file from disk:

`const BYTES: &[u8] = include_bytes!("Info.plist");`A naïve approach is to do the following:

```
#[used] // Prevent optimizing out
#[link_section = "__TEXT,__info_plist"]
static PLIST: &[u8] = BYTES;
```
This doesn’t work because only the slice’s pointer and length that are
placed in `__TEXT,__info_plist`. The referenced bytes are still placed in
`__TEXT,__const`.

Instead, we need to arrive at the following:

```
#[used]
#[link_section = "__TEXT,__info_plist"]
static PLIST: [u8; N] = *BYTES;
```
We can get `N` by using [ len](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.slice.html#method.len). As of Rust 1.39, it is possible to get the
length of a slice within a

`const`.`const N: usize = BYTES.len();`The next step is to dereference the bytes into a `[u8; N]`.

There are two approaches:

-
`include_bytes!`This is not the approach used by this library because of concerns about compile performance. See the [second approach](https://docs.rs#approach-2)for what this library does.The following is all we need: `#[used] #[link_section = "__TEXT,__info_plist"] static PLIST: [u8; N] = *include_bytes!("Info.plist");`This works because `include_bytes!`actually returns a`&[u8; N]`. It’s often used as a`&[u8]`because we don’t know the size when calling it.
-
This is tricker than the [first approach](https://docs.rs#approach-1)(and somewhat cursed). If you know me, then it’s predictable I’d go this route.We can get a pointer to the bytes via `as_ptr``const`:`const PTR: *const [u8; N] = BYTES.as_ptr() as *const [u8; N];`Unfortunately, this pointer can’t be directly dereferenced in Rust 1.39 (minimum supported version). Instead, we must cast the pointer to a reference. You may want to reach for `transmute``const`in Rust 1.46. However, earlier versions need to be supported, so that is not an option for this library.This bitwise cast can be accomplished with a `union`:`union Transmute { from: *const [u8; N], into: &'static [u8; N], } const REF: &[u8; N] = unsafe { Transmute { from: PTR }.into };`Finally, we can dereference our bytes: `#[used] #[link_section = "__TEXT,__info_plist"] static PLIST: [u8; N] = *REF;`

[§](https://docs.rs#license)License

This project is released under either:

at your choosing.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [embed_](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_info_plist.html)- info_ - plist
- Embeds the `Info.plist``$path`directly in the current binary.
- [embed_](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_info_plist_bytes.html)- info_ - plist_ - bytes
- Embeds the `Info.plist``&[u8]`directly in the current binary.
- [embed_](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_launchd_plist.html)- launchd_ - plist
- Embeds the `launchd.plist``$path`directly in the current binary.
- [embed_](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_launchd_plist_bytes.html)- launchd_ - plist_ - bytes
- Embeds the `launchd.plist``&[u8]`directly in the current binary.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [get_](https://docs.rs/fn.get_info_plist.html)- info_ - plist
- Returns the contents of the embedded `Info.plist`
- [get_](https://docs.rs/fn.get_launchd_plist.html)- launchd_ - plist
- Returns the contents of the embedded `launchd.plist`

# get_info_plist in embed_plist - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/embed_plist/latest/target-redirect/embed_plist/fn.get_info_plist.html

`pub fn get_info_plist() -> &'static [`[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u8.html)]## Expand description

Returns the contents of the embedded [ Info.plist](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/General/Reference/InfoPlistKeyReference/Introduction/Introduction.html) file.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

We can verify that the result is correct by checking it against the file at runtime:

```
embed_plist::embed_info_plist!("Info.plist");

assert_eq!(embedded_plist, read_plist.as_slice());
```
If `embed_info_plist!` has not been called, this function creates a
compile-time error by failing to reference the symbol defined by that macro:

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

This function relies on `_EMBED_INFO_PLIST` being defined within the
`__TEXT,__info_plist` section. You **should not** define this symbol outside
of using the macros provided by this library.

# embed_info_plist_bytes in embed_plist - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/embed_plist/latest/target-redirect/embed_plist/macro.embed_info_plist_bytes.html

```
macro_rules! embed_info_plist_bytes {
    ($bytes:expr) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Embeds the [ Info.plist](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/General/Reference/InfoPlistKeyReference/Introduction/Introduction.html) file in

`&[u8]` directly in the current binary.This enables you to have more control over what bytes are embedded into your
program. For example, you may want to do `const`-compatible preprocessing
such as converting into a binary property list.

The [ embed_info_plist!](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_info_plist.html) macro is a convenience wrapper around this and

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/macro.include_bytes.html)

`include_bytes!`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

After using this macro, you can get its content by calling
[ get_info_plist](https://docs.rs/fn.get_info_plist.html) from anywhere in your program:

```
const PLIST: &[u8] = r#"
    <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
    <!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
    <plist version="1.0">
    <dict>
        <key>Why</key>
        <string>To use in doc tests</string>
    </dict>
    </plist>
"#.as_bytes();
embed_plist::embed_info_plist_bytes!(PLIST);
let embedded = embed_plist::get_info_plist();
assert_eq!(embedded, PLIST);
```

---

# clap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/clap

## Expand description

Command Line Argument Parser for Rust

Quick Links:

- Derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)
- Builder [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html)
- [Cookbook](https://docs.rs/_cookbook/index.html)
- [CLI Concepts](https://docs.rs/_concepts/index.html)
- [FAQ](https://docs.rs/_faq/index.html)
- [Discussions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions)
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/blob/v4.6.1/CHANGELOG.md)(includes major version migration guides)

[§](https://docs.rs#aspirations)Aspirations

- Out of the box, users get a polished CLI experience
- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output, [shell completions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/tree/master/clap_complete), etc

- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output,
- Flexible enough to port your existing CLI interface
- However, we won’t necessarily streamline support for each use case

- Reasonable parse performance
- Resilient maintainership, including
- Willing to break compatibility rather than batching up breaking changes in large releases
- Leverage feature flags to keep to one active branch
- Being under [WG-CLI](https://github.com/rust-cli/team/)to increase the bus factor

- We follow semver and will wait about 6-9 months between major breaking changes
- We will support the last two minor Rust releases (MSRV, currently 1.74)

While these aspirations can be at odds with fast build times and low binary
size, we will still strive to keep these reasonable for the flexibility you
get.  Check out the
[argparse-benchmarks](https://github.com/rust-cli/argparse-benchmarks-rs) for
CLI parsers optimized for other use cases.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Run

`$ cargo add clap --features derive`*(See also  feature flag reference)*

Then define your CLI in `main.rs`:

```
use clap::Parser;
/// Simple program to greet a person
#[derive(Parser, Debug)]
#[command(version, about, long_about = None)]
struct Args {
    /// Name of the person to greet
    #[arg(short, long)]
    name: String,
    /// Number of times to greet
    #[arg(short, long, default_value_t = 1)]
    count: u8,
}
fn main() {
    let args = Args::parse();
    for _ in 0..args.count {
        println!("Hello {}!", args.name);
    }
}
```
And try it out:

```
$ demo --help
A simple to use, efficient, and full-featured Command Line Argument Parser
Usage: demo[EXE] [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>
Options:
  -n, --name <NAME>    Name of the person to greet
  -c, --count <COUNT>  Number of times to greet [default: 1]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
$ demo --name Me
Hello Me!
```
*(version number and  .exe extension on windows replaced by placeholders)*

See also the derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html) and [reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)

# clap - Rust

Command Line Argument Parser for Rust

[§](https://docs.rs#aspirations)Aspirations

- Out of the box, users get a polished CLI experience
- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output, [shell completions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/tree/master/clap_complete), etc

- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output,
- Flexible enough to port your existing CLI interface
- However, we won’t necessarily streamline support for each use case

- Reasonable parse performance
- Resilient maintainership, including
- Willing to break compatibility rather than batching up breaking changes in large releases
- Leverage feature flags to keep to one active branch
- Being under [WG-CLI](https://github.com/rust-cli/team/)to increase the bus factor

- We follow semver and will wait about 6-9 months between major breaking changes
- We will support the last two minor Rust releases (MSRV, currently 1.74)

While these aspirations can be at odds with fast build times and low binary
size, we will still strive to keep these reasonable for the flexibility you
get.  Check out the
[argparse-benchmarks](https://github.com/rust-cli/argparse-benchmarks-rs) for
CLI parsers optimized for other use cases.

```

Options:
