## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [broadcast](https://docs.rs/fn.broadcast.html)
- Executes `op`within every thread in the current thread pool. If this is called from a non-Rayon thread, it will execute in the global thread pool. Any attempts to use`join`,`scope`, or parallel iterators will then operate within that thread pool. When the call has completed on each thread, returns a vector containing all of their return values.
- [current_](https://docs.rs/fn.current_num_threads.html)- num_ - threads
- Returns the number of threads in the current registry. If this code is executing within a Rayon thread pool, then this will be the number of threads for the thread pool of the current thread. Otherwise, it will be the number of threads for the global thread pool.
- [current_](https://docs.rs/fn.current_thread_index.html)- thread_ - index
- If called from a Rayon worker thread, returns the index of that
thread within its current pool; if not called from a Rayon thread,
returns `None`.
- [in_](https://docs.rs/fn.in_place_scope.html)- place_ - scope
- Creates a “fork-join” scope `s`and invokes the closure with a reference to`s`. This closure can then spawn asynchronous tasks into`s`. Those tasks may run asynchronously with respect to the closure; they may themselves spawn additional tasks into`s`. When the closure returns, it will block until all tasks that have been spawned into`s`complete.
- [in_](https://docs.rs/fn.in_place_scope_fifo.html)- place_ - scope_ - fifo
- Creates a “fork-join” scope `s`with FIFO order, and invokes the closure with a reference to`s`. This closure can then spawn asynchronous tasks into`s`. Those tasks may run asynchronously with respect to the closure; they may themselves spawn additional tasks into`s`. When the closure returns, it will block until all tasks that have been spawned into`s`complete.
- [join](https://docs.rs/fn.join.html)
- Takes two closures and *potentially*runs them in parallel. It returns a pair of the results from those closures.
- [join_](https://docs.rs/fn.join_context.html)- context
- Identical to `join`, except that the closures have a parameter that provides context for the way the closure has been called, especially indicating whether they’re executing on a different thread than where`join_context`was called. This will occur if the second job is stolen by a different thread, or if`join_context`was called from outside the thread pool to begin with.
- [max_](https://docs.rs/fn.max_num_threads.html)- num_ - threads
- Returns the maximum number of threads that Rayon supports in a single thread pool.
- [scope](https://docs.rs/fn.scope.html)
- Creates a “fork-join” scope `s`and invokes the closure with a reference to`s`. This closure can then spawn asynchronous tasks into`s`. Those tasks may run asynchronously with respect to the closure; they may themselves spawn additional tasks into`s`. When the closure returns, it will block until all tasks that have been spawned into`s`complete.
- [scope_](https://docs.rs/fn.scope_fifo.html)- fifo
- Creates a “fork-join” scope `s`with FIFO order, and invokes the closure with a reference to`s`. This closure can then spawn asynchronous tasks into`s`. Those tasks may run asynchronously with respect to the closure; they may themselves spawn additional tasks into`s`. When the closure returns, it will block until all tasks that have been spawned into`s`complete.
- [spawn](https://docs.rs/fn.spawn.html)
- Puts the task into the Rayon thread pool’s job queue in the “static”
or “global” scope. Just like a standard thread, this task is not
tied to the current stack frame, and hence it cannot hold any
references other than those with `'static`lifetime. If you want to spawn a task that references stack data, use[the](https://docs.rs/fn.scope.html)to create a scope.`scope()`function
- [spawn_](https://docs.rs/fn.spawn_broadcast.html)- broadcast
- Spawns an asynchronous task on every thread in this thread pool. This task
will run in the implicit, global scope, which means that it may outlast the
current stack frame – therefore, it cannot capture any references onto the
stack (you will likely need a `move`closure).
- [spawn_](https://docs.rs/fn.spawn_fifo.html)- fifo
- Fires off a task into the Rayon thread pool in the “static” or
“global” scope.  Just like a standard thread, this task is not
tied to the current stack frame, and hence it cannot hold any
references other than those with `'static`lifetime. If you want to spawn a task that references stack data, use[the](https://docs.rs/fn.scope_fifo.html)to create a scope.`scope_fifo()`function
- [yield_](https://docs.rs/fn.yield_local.html)- local
- Cooperatively yields execution to local Rayon work.
- [yield_](https://docs.rs/fn.yield_now.html)- now
- Cooperatively yields execution to Rayon.

---

# facett_docview - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/facett-docview/0.1.10/target-redirect/facett_docview/

## Expand description

**facett-docview** — a documentation viewer. Render a **Typst-authored manual**
exported as **one vector SVG per page** inside egui, with a table-of-contents
sidebar and continuous vertical scrolling — **pure Rust**, no pdfium / no
native libraries.

The pipeline is [resvg](https://docs.rs/resvg/0.47.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/resvg/index.html)/[usvg](https://docs.rs/usvg/0.47.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/usvg/index.html)/[tiny_skia](https://docs.rs/tiny-skia/0.12.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tiny_skia/index.html) (all re-exported from `resvg`):

- Each page’s SVG bytes are parsed **once**at construction (`usvg::Tree::from_data`**no**font database. But facett-docview also renders SVGs that carry real`<text>`(e.g. skade’s diagrams), and usvg silently**drops**. So we parse with a`<text>`it cannot shape without a font`usvg::Options``fontdb`is populated (see`shared_fontdb`): system fonts**plus**a small embedded open font (DejaVu Sans,`assets/DejaVuSans.ttf`) set as the default family, so text shapes + renders**even on an airgapped box with zero system fonts**(the nordisk offline-manual ethos). The database is built**once**and shared (an`Arc`) across every page parse — never reloaded per page. Pre-outlined (Typst) pages parse fine through the same options; they simply never touch the fontdb.
- To show a page at the current zoom we compute `target_px = page_pt * zoom * pixels_per_point`, allocate a`tiny_skia::Pixmap``tiny_skia::Transform``resvg::render``egui::ColorImage``ctx.load_texture`, and draw it with`ui.image()`.
- A **texture cache**keyed by`(page_index, zoom_bucket)`re-rasterizes a page**only when its zoom bucket changes**— never every frame. Only pages in or near the viewport rasterize; far-offscreen textures are dropped to bound memory. Zoom and the per-page texture dimension are both clamped.

Source-agnostic: the host hands [ DocView::new](https://docs.rs/struct.DocView.html#method.new) a

`Vec<DocPage>` (each a page’s
SVG bytes) and a table of contents (`Vec<(title, page_index)>`). It implements
the canonical [so it drops into a](https://docs.rs/trait.Facet.html)

`facett_core::Facet``FacetDeck` and exposes
everything it renders via [(LAW 6).](https://docs.rs/trait.Facet.html#tymethod.state_json)

`Facet::state_json`## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [DocPage](https://docs.rs/struct.DocPage.html)
- One page of the manual: its source SVG, parsed once into a `usvg::Tree`
- [DocView](https://docs.rs/struct.DocView.html)
- A documentation viewer: a stack of vector SVG pages with a TOC sidebar, continuous scrolling, stepped zoom + fit-width, and a page-jump box.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [MAX_](https://docs.rs/constant.MAX_TEX_DIM.html)- TEX_ - DIM
- A rasterized page’s pixmap is never allowed to exceed this in either dimension (bounds memory even at MAX_ZOOM on a hi-dpi screen).
- [MAX_](https://docs.rs/constant.MAX_ZOOM.html)- ZOOM
- Maximum zoom — see `MIN_ZOOM`
- [MIN_](https://docs.rs/constant.MIN_ZOOM.html)- ZOOM
- Zoom is clamped to this range (a stepped zoom in/out + fit-width all clamp here).
- [PAGE_](https://docs.rs/constant.PAGE_GAP.html)- GAP
- Vertical gap between stacked pages, in logical points.
- [ZOOM_](https://docs.rs/constant.ZOOM_STEP.html)- STEP
- Stepped zoom multiplier for the +/- buttons.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Facet](https://docs.rs/trait.Facet.html)
- The facett **component contract**. Every facet — graph, map, pipeline, table, the ported nornir viewers — implements this, so consumers (korp, nornir, …) compose them uniformly*and*get headless robot-testing for free.
- [Page](https://docs.rs/trait.PageSource.html)- Source
- A source of page SVG bytes, fetched **on demand**by 0-based index. The host implements this (e.g. over a compressed/archived manual) and the viewer pulls only the pages the viewport needs — so a huge manual never parses or holds all pages at once. Must be`Send + Sync`: the viewer fetches + parses the needed pages in parallel (rayon, 1 page per core).

---

# usvg - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/usvg/0.47.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/usvg/index.html

## Expand description

`usvg` (micro SVG) is an [SVG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scalable_Vector_Graphics) parser that tries to solve most of SVG complexity.

SVG is notoriously hard to parse. `usvg` presents a layer between an XML library and
a potential SVG rendering library. It will parse an input SVG into a strongly-typed tree structure
were all the elements, attributes, references and other SVG features are already resolved
and presented in the simplest way possible.
So a caller doesn’t have to worry about most of the issues related to SVG parsing
and can focus just on the rendering part.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- All supported attributes are resolved. No need to worry about inheritable, implicit and default attributes
- CSS will be applied
- Only simple paths
- Basic shapes (like `rect`and`circle`) will be converted into paths
- Paths contain only absolute *MoveTo*,*LineTo*,*QuadTo*,*CurveTo*and*ClosePath*segments. ArcTo, implicit and relative segments will be converted

- Basic shapes (like
- `use`will be resolved and replaced with the reference content
- Nested `svg`will be resolved
- Invalid, malformed elements will be removed
- Relative length units (mm, em, etc.) will be converted into pixels/points
- External images will be loaded
- Internal, base64 images will be decoded
- All references (like `#elem`and`url(#elem)`) will be resolved
- `switch`will be resolved
- Text elements, which are probably the hardest part of SVG, will be completely resolved.
This includes all the attributes resolving, whitespaces preprocessing (`xml:space`), text chunks and spans resolving
- Markers will be converted into regular elements. No need to place them manually
- All filters are supported. Including filter functions, like `filter="contrast(50%)"`
- Recursive elements will be detected and removed
- `objectBoundingBox`will be replaced with- `userSpaceOnUse`

[§](https://docs.rs#limitations)Limitations

- Unsupported SVG features will be ignored
- CSS support is minimal
- Only [static](http://www.w3.org/TR/SVG11/feature#SVG-static)SVG features, e.g. no`a`,`view`,`cursor`,`script`, no events and no animations

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [fontdb](https://docs.rs/fontdb/0.23.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/fontdb/index.html);
- `pub use`- [strict_num](https://docs.rs/strict-num/0.1.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/strict_num/index.html);

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Approx](https://docs.rs/trait.ApproxEqUlps.html)- EqUlps
- ApproxEqUlps is a trait for approximate equality comparisons. The associated type Flt is a floating point type which implements Ulps, and is required so that this trait can be implemented for compound types (e.g. vectors), not just for the floats themselves.
- [Approx](https://docs.rs/trait.ApproxZeroUlps.html)- Zero - Ulps
- Approximate zero equality comparisons.

# DocView in facett_docview - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/facett-docview/0.1.10/facett_docview/struct.DocView.html

```
pub struct DocView {
    pub title:
```
[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    /* private fields */
}## Expand description

A documentation viewer: a stack of vector SVG pages with a TOC sidebar, continuous scrolling, stepped zoom + fit-width, and a page-jump box.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

#### pub fn [from_source](https://docs.rs#method.from_source)(
    title: impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
    source: [Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)<dyn [PageSource](https://docs.rs/trait.PageSource.html)>,
    toc: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<([String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html), [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html))>,
) -> Self

Build a **lazy** viewer over a [ PageSource](https://docs.rs/trait.PageSource.html): pages are fetched + parsed
only as they scroll near the viewport, and dropped when they leave it — so
a huge manual (hundreds of MB of SVG) opens instantly and never holds more
than the visible band in memory. The host supplies bytes by index (e.g.
from a compressed archive with O(1) per-entry reads); the viewer never sees
the storage. The TOC is taken verbatim.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/facett_docview/lib.rs.html#383-400)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/facett_docview/lib.rs.html#383-400)

Build a viewer by parsing each page’s raw SVG bytes. Pages that fail to
parse are skipped (returned in the `Err`-count via [ DocView::page_count](https://docs.rs/struct.DocView.html#method.page_count)
vs. the input length); the TOC is taken verbatim. This is the host-friendly
constructor for

`include_bytes!`-bundled manuals.Set zoom, clamped to `[MIN_ZOOM, MAX_ZOOM]`. Returns the applied value.

Fit the first page’s width into `panel_width` logical px (`zoom = panel_width / page_width_pt`), clamped. No-op (returns current zoom) when
there are no pages.

Request a scroll to `page` (0-based, clamped) on the next render — the
programmatic equivalent of clicking its TOC entry.

Toggle the TOC sidebar.

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

The uniform scale IS the zoom — so the deck’s zoom toolbar/shortcuts drive
the same value `fit_width`/`zoom_in` do.

[portable_state](https://docs.rs#method.portable_state)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Value](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.150/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_json/value/enum.Value.html)> { ... }
[load_state](https://docs.rs#method.load_state)(&mut self, _state: &[Value](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.150/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_json/value/enum.Value.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) { ... }
}## Expand description

The facett **component contract**. Every facet — graph, map, pipeline, table,
the ported nornir viewers — implements this, so consumers (korp, nornir, …)
compose them uniformly *and* get headless robot-testing for free.

The three things a component owes its host:

- a **title**(tab label / panel heading),
- how to **draw**itself into egui,
- its **observable state**as JSON — dumped to`$APP_STATE`for headless assertions.**Rule:**every visible list/status/count goes in`state_json`.

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Provided Methods[§](https://docs.rs#provided-methods)

Set the uniform scale; clamp internally. Default no-op (not scalable).

Clipboard hooks — see clipboard.rs. Defaults: nothing to give/take. Returns the text to place on the clipboard (None = nothing copyable now).

Optional downcast handle for hosts that need typed access to a specific
facet living inside a [ FacetDeck](https://docs.rs/facett-core/0.1.10/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/facett_core/struct.FacetDeck.html) (e.g. a robot-UI driver clicking an
app-level control that must forward to a concrete component’s own API).
Defaulted to

`None` so no existing facet has to change; a component opts in
by returning `Some(self)`.Stable component-type id (e.g. `"jobview"`, `"graphpan"`, `"table"`). Two
instances with the **same** kind can exchange portable state; the empty
default `""` means **opted out** of cross-instance clone.

Parse one page’s SVG bytes into a [ DocPage](https://docs.rs/struct.DocPage.html). The parse

[carry a populated](https://docs.rs/usvg/0.47.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/usvg/parser/options/struct.Options.html)

`usvg::Options``fontdb` ([`shared_fontdb`]: system fonts + an embedded
fallback) and a default family, so SVGs with real `<text>` (skade’s
diagrams) shape + render — usvg would otherwise **drop**unshapeable text. Pre-outlined (Typst) pages parse identically; they just never use the fontdb. The shared

`Arc<fontdb::Database>` is cloned (cheap), never rebuilt.
Returns the usvg parse error on malformed SVG (the host can skip a bad page).[Source](https://docs.rs/src/facett_docview/lib.rs.html#147-168)#### pub fn [rasterize](https://docs.rs#method.rasterize)(&self, scale: [f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f32.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[ColorImage](https://docs.rs/epaint/0.34.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/epaint/image/struct.ColorImage.html)>

# PageSource in facett_docview - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/facett-docview/0.1.10/facett_docview/trait.PageSource.html

`pub trait PageSource: `[Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html) + [Sync](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sync.html) {
    // Required methods
    fn [page_count](https://docs.rs#tymethod.page_count)(&self) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html);
[page_svg](https://docs.rs#tymethod.page_svg)(&self, i: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>>;
    // Provided method
    fn [page_size_hint](https://docs.rs#method.page_size_hint)(&self) -> ([f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f32.html), [f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f32.html)) { ... }
}## Expand description

A source of page SVG bytes, fetched **on demand** by 0-based index. The host
implements this (e.g. over a compressed/archived manual) and the viewer pulls
only the pages the viewport needs — so a huge manual never parses or holds all
pages at once. Must be `Send + Sync`: the viewer fetches + parses the needed
pages in parallel (rayon, 1 page per core).

This is the ONLY seam the viewer exposes for lazy loading — it knows nothing
about where the bytes come from (file, archive, network); it just asks for
page `i` when `i` scrolls near the viewport.

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Provided Methods[§](https://docs.rs#provided-methods)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/facett_docview/lib.rs.html#189-191)#### fn [page_size_hint](https://docs.rs#method.page_size_hint)(&self) -> ([f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f32.html), [f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f32.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/facett_docview/lib.rs.html#189-191)

#### fn [page_size_hint](https://docs.rs#method.page_size_hint)(&self) -> ([f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f32.html), [f32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f32.html))

Optional size hint (width_pt, height_pt) used to lay out not-yet-parsed pages so the scrollbar is stable before they’re fetched. Defaults to A4 portrait (595×842 pt) — exact for a uniform typst manual; refined from the first parsed page regardless.

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

# facett-console 0.1.10 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/facett-console/0.1.10

**facett-console** (§8 TYPE-2) — a themed terminal/shell component: a fixed
**monospace cell grid**, a block/beam **cursor**, optional **ANSI** colour
mapped to the palette, and **scrollback** on the CygnusEd smooth-scroll engine
(§11). A [`Facet`]: themeable · resizable · scalable · copyable · searchable.

Lines are appended by the host (a process' stdout, a REPL); the console owns
the scrollback ring + the smooth-scroll offset (deterministic under an
injected clock via `advance`). ANSI SGR colour codes (30–37/90–97) map onto
the active [ Theme](https://docs.rs/facett_core::Theme) so the terminal matches the app.

---

# facett_console - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/facett-console/0.1.10/facett_console/index.html

## Expand description

**facett-console** (§8 TYPE-2) — a themed terminal/shell component: a fixed
**monospace cell grid**, a block/beam **cursor**, optional **ANSI** colour
mapped to the palette, and **scrollback** on the CygnusEd smooth-scroll engine
(§11). A [ Facet](https://docs.rs/facett-core/0.1.10/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/facett_core/trait.Facet.html): themeable · resizable · scalable · copyable · searchable.

Lines are appended by the host (a process’ stdout, a REPL); the console owns
the scrollback ring + the smooth-scroll offset (deterministic under an
injected clock via `advance`). ANSI SGR colour codes (30–37/90–97) map onto
the active [ Theme](https://docs.rs/facett-core/0.1.10/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/facett_core/theme/struct.Theme.html) so the terminal matches the app.

[83](#83)    let mut spans = Vec::new();
[84](#84)    let mut cur = String::new();
[85](#85)    let mut color: Option<AnsiColor> = None;
[86](#86)    let bytes = line.as_bytes();
[87](#87)    let mut i = 0;
[88](#88)    while i < bytes.len() {
[89](#89)        if bytes[i] == 0x1b && i + 1 < bytes.len() && bytes[i + 1] == b'[' {
[90](#90)            if !cur.is_empty() {
[92](#92)                spans.push(Span { text: std::mem::take(&mut cur), color });
[93](#93)            }
[94](#94)            let mut j = i + 2;
[96](#96)            let mut num = String::new();
[97](#97)            while j < bytes.len() && bytes[j] != b'm' {
[98](#98)                num.push(bytes[j] as char);
[99](#99)                j += 1;
[100](#100)            }
[101](#101)            if let Some(code) = num.split(';').next_back().and_then(|s| s.parse::<u8>().ok()) {
[103](#103)                if code == 0 {
[104](#104)                    color = None;
[105](#105)                } else if (30..=37).contains(&code) || (90..=97).contains(&code) {
[106](#106)                    color = AnsiColor::from_sgr(code);
[107](#107)                }
[108](#108)            }
[109](#109)            i = j + 1;
[110](#110)        } else {
[111](#111)            cur.push(bytes[i] as char);
[112](#112)            i += 1;
[113](#113)        }
[114](#114)    }
[115](#115)    if !cur.is_empty() || spans.is_empty() {
[116](#116)        spans.push(Span { text: cur, color });
[117](#117)    }
[118](#118)    spans
[119](#119)}
[120](#120)

[236](#236)    fn ui(&mut self, ui: &mut Ui) {
[237](#237)        let th = theme(ui);
[238](#238)        let cell_h = 16.0 * self.scale;
[239](#239)        let font = FontId::monospace(13.0 * self.scale);
[240](#240)
[241](#241)        let total_h = self.lines.len() as f32 * cell_h;
[243](#243)        let (rect, _) = ui.allocate_exact_size(vec2(ui.available_width(), ui.available_height().max(cell_h * 3.0)), Sense::hover());
[244](#244)        let view_h = rect.height();
[245](#245)        self.scroll.set_max((total_h - view_h).max(0.0));
[246](#246)
[247](#247)        let painter = ui.painter_at(rect);
[248](#248)        painter.rect_filled(rect, 0.0, th.bg);
[249](#249)
[250](#250)        let (first, frac) = self.scroll.first_row_and_frac(cell_h);
[252](#252)        let visible = (view_h / cell_h).ceil() as usize + 1;
[253](#253)        for vi in 0..visible {
[254](#254)            let li = first + vi;
[255](#255)            if li >= self.lines.len() {
[256](#256)                break;
[257](#257)            }
[258](#258)            let y = rect.top() + vi as f32 * cell_h - frac;
[259](#259)            let mut x = rect.left() + 4.0;
[260](#260)            for span in &self.lines[li] {
[261](#261)                let color = span.color.map(|c| c.to_color(&th)).unwrap_or(th.text);
[262](#262)                let g = painter.layout_no_wrap(span.text.clone(), font.clone(), color);
[263](#263)                let w = g.size().x;
[264](#264)                painter.galley(pos2(x, y), g, color);
[265](#265)                x += w;
[266](#266)            }
[267](#267)        }
[268](#268)
[269](#269)        let py = rect.bottom() - cell_h;
[271](#271)        let prompt_text = format!("{}{}", self.prompt, self.input);
[272](#272)        let pg = painter.layout_no_wrap(prompt_text.clone(), font.clone(), th.accent);
[273](#273)        painter.galley(pos2(rect.left() + 4.0, py), pg, th.accent);
[274](#274)        let cw = font.size * 0.6;
[276](#276)        let cx = rect.left() + 4.0 + prompt_text.chars().count() as f32 * cw;
[277](#277)        let crect = Rect::from_min_size(pos2(cx, py), vec2(cw, cell_h));
[278](#278)        match self.cursor {
[279](#279)            Cursor::Block => {
[280](#280)                painter.rect_filled(crect, 0.0, th.accent.linear_multiply(0.5));
[281](#281)            }
[282](#282)            Cursor::Beam => {
[283](#283)                painter.line_segment([crect.left_top(), crect.left_bottom()], Stroke::new(2.0, th.accent));
[284](#284)            }
[285](#285)            Cursor::Underline => {
[286](#286)                painter.line_segment([crect.left_bottom(), crect.right_bottom()], Stroke::new(2.0, th.accent));
[287](#287)            }
[288](#288)        }
[289](#289)        let _ = Align2::LEFT_TOP;
[290](#290)
[291](#291)        let base = ui.id().with("console");
[301](#301)        let input_rect = Rect::from_min_size(pos2(rect.left(), py), vec2(rect.width(), cell_h));
[302](#302)        let input_id = stable_id(base, "input");
[303](#303)        let input_resp = ui.interact(input_rect, input_id, Sense::click());
[304](#304)        let typed = self.input.clone();
[305](#305)        input_resp.widget_info(|| egui::WidgetInfo::text_edit(true, "", &typed, "console input"));
[306](#306)
[307](#307)        let count = self.lines.len();
[311](#311)        let scrollback_rect = Rect::from_min_max(rect.min, pos2(rect.right(), py));
[312](#312)        a11y_node(
[313](#313)            ui,
[314](#314)            base,
[315](#315)            "scrollback",
[316](#316)            Sense::hover(),
[317](#317)            scrollback_rect,
[318](#318)            Semantics::new(WidgetType::Label, format!("console — {count} lines")).value(count as f64),
[319](#319)        );
[320](#320)
[321](#321)        #[cfg(feature = "testmatrix")]
[323](#323)        facett_core::testmatrix::emit(
[324](#324)            "facett-console::Console::ui",
[325](#325)            "ui_render",
[326](#326)            count == self.lines.len() && self.lines.len() <= self.max_lines,
[329](#329)            &format!(
[330](#330)                "lines={} max={} input_len={} scroll_max={}",
[331](#331)                self.lines.len(),
[332](#332)                self.max_lines,
[333](#333)                self.input.chars().count(),
[334](#334)                self.scroll.max,
[335](#335)            ),
[336](#336)        );
[337](#337)    }

}## Expand description

The facett palette. All custom-painted colours come from here.

`glow` is the colour the [ effects](https://docs.rs/effects/index.html) module blooms with
(layered alpha strokes). It defaults to

`accent` for the legacy palettes via
the constructors below, but a striking theme may pick a distinct glow.## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

`glow: `[Color32](https://docs.rs/ecolor/0.34.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/ecolor/color32/struct.Color32.html)## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Every named theme, in picker order. Drives a UI/CLI palette switcher.

Look a theme up by its `name` (case-insensitive; `-`/`_`/spaces are
interchangeable, so `"nordic aurora"`, `"nordic-aurora"`, `"Nordic_Aurora"`
all match). `None` if unknown.

Neon-on-near-black — a sci-fi HUD look (cyan/magenta on deep blue-black).

**Nordic aurora** — deep fjord-night blue with green/teal aurora ribbons
and a cold violet accent. Calm but luminous; the glow is aurora-green.

**Cyberpunk neon** — hot magenta + electric cyan on bruised purple-black.
Maximum night-city pop; the glow is magenta.

**Amber CRT** — a warm phosphor terminal: amber-on-black with a dim
scan-line brown. Cosy retro; the glow is amber.

Append a raw line (ANSI-parsed), dropping the oldest past `max_lines`.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/facett_console/lib.rs.html#175-177)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/facett_console/lib.rs.html#178-180)

#### pub fn [line_count](https://docs.rs#method.line_count)(&self) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)

Whether the console is idle (FC-8). The console is host-pushed and
synchronous — lines arrive via [ push_line](https://docs.rs/struct.Console.html#method.push_line) on the host’s
thread and there is no internal async work — so it is always idle from the
component’s own perspective.
